description.narrative: The objective of the Balochistan Human Capital Investment Project for Pakistan is to improve utilization of quality health and education services in selected refugee hosting districts of Balochistan. The Project has two components. 1. Improving utilization of quality health services component will improve utilization of quality health services. 1.1. Improving delivery of quality health services subcomponent will support improving delivery of quality health services in selected refugee hosting districts, with a focus on Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn, Child Health, and Nutrition (RMNCHN). 1.2. Strengthening health sector stewardship subcomponent will support strengthening health sector stewardship in selected refugee hosting districts. 2. Improving utilization of quality education services component improve utilization of quality education services among children, especially girls, by increasing access to quality education services and strengthening education sector stewardship. 2.1. Improving delivery of primary and secondary education subcomponent will support improving delivery of primary and secondary education in selected refugee hosting districts. 2.2. Strengthening education sector stewardship subcomponent will support strengthening education sector stewardship in selected refugee hosting districts. This subcomponent will support interventions to improve quality of learning. To improve the resilience in public service delivery in case of climatic extremes, the project will integrate climate change considerations in its design.
To improve utilization of quality health and education services in selected refugee hosting districts of Balochistan.

condition.narrative: The Project Implementing Entity shall carry out the Project in accordance with the Implementation Arrangements set out in Section Iof the Schedule of the Project Agreement.

title.narrative: Targeted schools meeting at least 3 model school criteria

comment.narrative: 268 schools meet the required 3 of 5 model schools criteria. The project target is 207 schools

title.narrative: Targeted school clusters with improved cluster-based governance
Grievances registered related to delivery of project benefits that are addressed

comment.narrative: The health and education component received a total of 117 complaints, comprising 97 related to health and 20 to education. All complaints have been successfully addressed and resolved through the established GRM process.
The teachers have been trained in the female target project schools. The target has been achieved.

title.narrative: Targeted health care providers with minimum knowledge and competencies in RMNCHN services

comment.narrative: Target of 400 individuals have been achieved.

title.narrative: Students benefiting from direct interventions to enhance learning
People who have received essential health, nutrition, and population (HNP) services
Targeted HMIS digitally integrated into DHIS(2)

comment.narrative: The Nutrition Program, MNCH Program, Family Planning & EPI have been integrated into the DHIS-II and implemented in all project's districts.

title.narrative: Grade 5 and 8 students scoring at least 50% in concept-based learning assessment in project schools

comment.narrative: The baseline has been completed and the endline is currently in progress. It is expected to be completed before the project's closing date.

title.narrative: Female students enrolled in project schools
Targeted HFs having majority of essential medicines for RMNCHN services

comment.narrative: Quarterly supplies are ensured in all focused Health Facilities.

title.narrative: Absenteeism among key staff to provide RMNCHN services

comment.narrative: Focused Health Facilities Staff Absenteeism has been reduced from to 25%.

title.narrative: Student learning assessment reforms strategy implemented

target.value: Dissemination of assessment results from 10% target primary schools

comment.narrative: The strategy has been developed and approved.
